339e5df84868b38b4772.text: IF-CLAUSE RESULT-CLAUSE 1. If I had phoned you last night, I would have reminded you to stay. 2. If it had rained hard, I might have not visited your place. 3. If she had taken her medicine, she could have felt better.

29bad49f8fde70545f65.text: If the “if”-clause comes first, a comma (,) is usually used. However, if it comes

dbdcfa5ee71a86954c31.text: after the main clause, no need for a comma.
